file_edits.before: The study examines source-only model selection and fixed spectral sharing in cross-subject motor-imagery EEG. It combines a documented BNCI development programme with separately frozen binary evaluations on PhysioNet, Cho2017 and Lee2019_MI. Zero calibration is defined as absence of target-dependent parameter fitting or target-based model selection. Target labels used for metadata and scoring are distinguished from learning; participant-level uncertainty is retained throughout.
file_edits.after: The study examines source-only model selection and the transfer limits of fixed spectral-sharing pipelines. BNCI development analyses are followed by separately frozen binary evaluations on PhysioNet, Cho2017 and Lee2019_MI. Zero calibration means no target-dependent fitting or model selection; label use for metadata and scoring is distinguished from learning. Results and uncertainty are reported at participant level.
file_edits.rationale: Lead with the study question and person-level evidence instead of development-programme wording.

file_edits.before: The completed Q15 evaluation covers 52 Cho2017 and 54 Lee2019_MI participants under a prespecified common 21-channel adapter. The adverse result is reported directly. Comparisons reflect complete frozen pipelines, including their selected training durations.

file_edits.before: Journal of Neural Engineering provides a relevant audience for reliable BCI evaluation and physiological interpretation. The manuscript shows how source-only duration decisions can produce concentrated gains and how a fixed spectral-sharing pipeline can have lower balanced accuracy under frozen transfer. Its separate sensor-level analysis provides physiological context while retaining the limits of retrospective association. The study does not evaluate online assistive control, patients or rehabilitation outcomes.
file_edits.after: The contribution is an evaluation of source-only decision rules and their transfer limits, rather than a new decoding algorithm. Person-level development gains, frozen external contrasts and separate sensor-level descriptions show why an aggregate improvement need not imply broad benefit or a physiological decoder mechanism. These questions concern the reliability and interpretation of BCI evidence, fitting the scope of Journal of Neural Engineering. The study does not evaluate online assistive control, patients or rehabilitation outcomes.
file_edits.rationale: State the evidence-based contribution and journal fit without a performance or novelty superlative.

file_edits.before: The study developed source-only decoding procedures on nine BNCI2014_001 participants, then evaluated frozen binary decoders on separate external acquisition cohorts held out from fitting. Cross-provider participant identity nonoverlap was not independently established. The four-class development task, the Q14 binary PhysioNet evaluation, and the Q15 binary Cho2017/Lee2019_MI evaluation have different input contracts. Their balanced accuracies are reported separately. Neither a pooled accuracy across tasks nor a combined external participant-level significance test was specified.
file_edits.after: Source-only decoding procedures were developed on nine BNCI2014_001 participants and evaluated as frozen binary pipelines on separate external acquisition cohorts held out from fitting. Participant identity nonoverlap across providers was not independently established. The four-class development task, Q14 binary PhysioNet evaluation and Q15 binary Cho2017/Lee2019_MI evaluation use different input contracts, so balanced accuracies are reported separately. No pooled accuracy across tasks or combined external participant-level significance test was specified.
file_edits.rationale: Replace repeated prohibitions with a concrete account of task and cohort separation.

file_edits.after: The inventory distinguishes evaluated conditions, fitted models, reused endpoints, metadata audits and unsuccessful or unrun branches. file_edits.before: The shared μ/β intervention supplies two fixed filtered views to the same EEGNet and averages the two class-logit vectors. Cross-entropy is computed from the averaged logits during training; inference applies softmax to their average. The views are reshaped into one two-view mini-batch, so BatchNorm parameters and running statistics are shared as well as convolutional weights. Dropout is applied per view during training. This architecture is a spectral input and parameter-sharing constraint; it is not a learned attention mechanism, two independently trained networks, or probability averaging.
file_edits.after: The shared μ/β pipeline supplies two fixed filtered views to the same EEGNet and averages their class-logit vectors. Training cross-entropy is computed from the averaged logits; inference applies softmax to that average. Both views form one two-view mini-batch, sharing BatchNorm parameters and running statistics as well as convolutional weights. Dropout is applied per view during training. This imposes an input and parameter-sharing constraint. It does not learn attention, train two independent networks or average probabilities.
file_edits.rationale: Use pipeline language and explain the architecture directly without implying an isolated causal intervention.

file_edits.before: The declared input convention is **native numerical values interpreted as microvolts**. Provider file identities, hashes, shapes, channels, sampling grids, cues, and label conventions were audited, but physical export voltage calibration was not independently established. The original Cho hardware reference and hardware cue latency also remain unverified. Common-average referencing provides a declared numerical coordinate system; it does not authenticate the original hardware reference. Accordingly, Q15 is reported as `completed_with_calibration_limitations`, an operational adapter benchmark under its stated convention. Its amplitudes and between-dataset differences must not be used to claim verified voltage equivalence or a controlled acquisition mechanism.
file_edits.after: The declared convention is **native numerical values interpreted as microvolts**. Provider file identities, hashes, shapes, channels, sampling grids, cues and label conventions were audited; physical export voltage calibration was not independently established. The original Cho hardware reference and cue latency also remain unverified. Common-average referencing defines numerical coordinates without authenticating the original hardware reference. Q15 is therefore reported as `completed_with_calibration_limitations`: an adapter benchmark under a stated input convention. Amplitudes and between-dataset differences do not establish voltage equivalence or a controlled acquisition mechanism.
file_edits.rationale: Explain calibration limits without repetitive prohibitive language.

file_edits.before: For person i and neural seed s, balanced accuracy is one half of the sum of left-class and right-class recall. Lee's two sessions are pooled within person before calculating this metric; session-level scores are descriptive. The three seed-specific balanced accuracies are then averaged within person. Cohort balanced accuracy is the arithmetic mean of those person-level values, giving each person equal weight despite Cho's unequal trial counts. The primary paired effect is shared μ/β minus broad EEGNet within person. CSP4+LDA is contextual; it is not an additional primary hypothesis in the predeclared family.
file_edits.after: For person i and neural seed s, balanced accuracy is the mean of left-class and right-class recall. Lee sessions are pooled within person before scoring; session scores remain descriptive. The three seed-specific balanced accuracies are then averaged within person, and cohort balanced accuracy averages those person values equally despite Cho's unequal trial counts. The primary paired contrast is shared μ/β minus broad EEGNet within person. CSP4+LDA provides context and is outside the predeclared primary family.
file_edits.rationale: Make estimand and aggregation order easier to follow without changing units or metrics.

file_edits.before: Development comparisons share nine BNCI people and often reuse inner trajectories, checkpoints, source subsets, or endpoints. They describe sensitivity in this research programme, rather than a sequence of independent confirmatory experiments. Q14 and Q15 have distinct channel/window/reference contracts and must not be merged as unchanged-protocol replications. Neither the tested fixed frequency split nor a logit-average architecture establishes physiological source separation, artifact causality, domain-invariant representations, clinical benefit, or online deployment readiness. Future work could investigate calibrated acquisition metadata, prespecified hardware harmonization, independent cohorts, and causal preprocessing; such work has not been executed here.
file_edits.after: Development comparisons repeatedly use the same nine BNCI people and often reuse inner trajectories, checkpoints, source subsets or endpoints. They describe sensitivity within this development benchmark rather than independent confirmatory experiments. Q14 and Q15 have different channel/window/reference contracts and are not unchanged-protocol replications. The fixed frequency split and logit-average architecture establish neither physiological source separation nor artifact causality, domain invariance, clinical benefit or online readiness. Calibrated acquisition metadata, prespecified hardware harmonization, independent cohorts and causal preprocessing are questions for future work, not completed analyses.
file_edits.rationale: Replace programme wording with an explicit inferential limit and concise future-work statement.

file_edits.before: The baseline contains one Welch segment and the task three overlapping segments. Their estimator variances differ, and the concavity of the logarithm can create a positive dB offset even for stationary unchanged power. Overlapping task segments are correlated. Accordingly, this is a fixed-window descriptive change estimate, not an unbiased ERD estimator or a mechanistic test. The baseline is not redesigned after viewing results.
file_edits.after: The baseline has one Welch segment and the task three overlapping segments, with different estimator variances. Because the logarithm is concave, this difference can produce a positive dB offset even when stationary power is unchanged; overlap also correlates the task segments. The ratio is therefore a fixed-window descriptive estimate, not an unbiased ERD estimator or a mechanistic test. The baseline was not redesigned after results were inspected.
file_edits.rationale: Explain the estimator limitation causally and clearly without making a neural-mechanism claim.

suggestions.evidence: Internal mean-rank gain is concentrated in S3/S8; fixed-duration positive mean coexists with improvement in only four of nine participants.
suggestions.supported_message: Source-only selection is a fitting boundary, not a guarantee that development gains generalize uniformly across people.
suggestions.limit: Exploratory development; no new effect estimate or typical-person causal claim.

suggestions.evidence: Duration-controlled and matched-runtime controls are distinguished from reselected broad/shared comparisons; external complete pipelines have unequal durations.
suggestions.supported_message: Audit the decision rule and complete frozen pipeline together; do not attribute the contrast to spectral sharing alone.
suggestions.limit: This is an evaluation contribution, not a new DG architecture or factorial causal experiment.

suggestions.evidence: Cho adverse paired contrast and Lee uncertain contrast survive frozen protocol and independent computational validation.
suggestions.supported_message: Transfer evidence constrains the scope of favorable internal observations and gives a reproducible boundary to generalization claims.
suggestions.limit: No pooled-cohort effect, superiority/non-equivalence claim, or independent laboratory replication.

suggestions.contribution: Physiology as a boundary test for interpretation
suggestions.evidence: All signed descriptors and six correlations are retained; negative laterality can accompany positive constituent changes; unequal Welch windows are disclosed.
suggestions.supported_message: Sensor-level summaries can describe the recordings while showing why an association cannot be read as a decoder mechanism.
suggestions.limit: Post-outcome, BNCI-only, nine people, no p-values, no decoder feedback or attribution.

suggestions.evidence: Raw/event gates, separate source/inference freezes, saved predictions, checkpoint-state checks and independent saved-number/raw-FFT checks.
suggestions.supported_message: The release lets readers trace a stated claim from protocol and population to stored prediction and reported statistic.
suggestions.limit: Software auditability does not authenticate acquisition voltage or create a replication cohort.

suggestions.evidence: Frozen Q15 class recalls show lower left and higher right recall for shared input in both cohorts, with different balances between those opposing within-cohort changes; Lee has a small aggregate contrast.
suggestions.supported_message: The cohort mean alone hides the opposing changes in left- and right-class recall within each cohort. Reporting both recalls makes adverse and uncertain transfer interpretable without outcome-based tuning.
suggestions.limit: Descriptive pattern only; no added class-wise hypothesis test, acquisition-cause attribution, class-threshold tuning, or mechanistic inference.

suggestions.contribution: Separate participant heterogeneity from fixed-seed sensitivity
suggestions.evidence: External tables report person SD separately from within-person SD over three fixed seeds; shared-input seed dispersion exceeds broad-input dispersion in both Q15 cohorts.
suggestions.supported_message: Person variability and seed variability answer different reliability questions, and neither should be inflated into additional independent sample size.
suggestions.limit: Three fixed seeds do not estimate the population distribution of training randomness; no variance-component model or robustness guarantee.
